summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after being found lethargic at a rehab facility, where she had been off her baseline oxygen. Initial improvement with Narcan suggested opioid-related sedation, but further evaluation revealed multiple contributing factors: a recent increase in lithium dose, right lower lobe pneumonia, and possible hypoxia from a pleural effusion. She was treated with intravenous antibiotics, supplemental oxygen, and respiratory support. Her mental status improved significantly by hospital day 2. Lithium was restarted at a reduced dose per psychiatric consultation, and methadone was gradually resumed. She remained afebrile, with improving white blood cell count, and was discharged to extended care on oral antibiotics and adjusted medications. A new knee brace was fitted prior to discharge.
